lemma: L-F1 (counting annihilator with explicit witness). Let G: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^m be any map and d >= 0 with N_d(m) := sum_{k<=d} C(m,k) > 2^n. Then there is a nonzero multilinear GF(2) polynomial P in m variables, of degree <= d, with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x in {0,1}^n. Moreover, a point y in {0,1}^m with P(y) = 1 exists and is computable from P, and y is not in Im(G).
evidence: cm-adfa104de41b49fe (exact GF(2) minimal annihilator degree on Veronese maps n=4..7 and random quadratic maps n=4..9). The lemma itself is a proof, not an experiment.
proved_step: PROOF. (i) The functions x -> mon_S(G(x)), |S| <= d, are N_d(m) vectors in the GF(2)-space of all functions {0,1}^n -> GF(2), which has dimension 2^n. Since N_d(m) > 2^n they are linearly dependent, so some nonzero coefficient vector (c_S) gives P = sum c_S mon_S with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x. P is nonzero as a multilinear polynomial because distinct multilinear monomials are distinct functions on {0,1}^m. (ii) Choose S with c_S = 1 inclusion-minimal. Then P(1_S) = sum_{T subset S} c_T = c_S = 1, since no proper T subset S has c_T = 1. So y = 1_S satisfies P(y) = 1 and P(G(x)) = 0 for all x, hence y not in Im(G). Cost: Gaussian elimination on a 2^n x N_d(m) GF(2) matrix, i.e. O(2^n N_d(m)^2) bit operations. (iii) Efficiency caveat: this costs 2^n times a polynomial, which is the same order as enumerating the inputs, so it gives no saving over brute force by itself.

refuted_approach: Counting-only annihilator (L-F1, S0001): pigeonhole on N_d(m) > 2^n gives a nonzero degree-<=d annihilator with an explicit witness y not in Im(G), but the witness is found by Gaussian elimination on a 2^n x N_d(m) GF(2) matrix, i.e. time 2^n * poly, the same order as enumerating {0,1}^n. It gives no saving, so it does not discharge obligation (1). It is also a standard pigeonhole fact, so it does not count as progress.
evidence: cm-adfa104de41b49fe (d_min table: Veronese n=4..7 d_min=2; random quadratic n=4..9 d_min in {2,3}; at n=7, m=14, d_min=2 < counting threshold 3, so counting is not tight). The lemma is a proof, not an experiment.
